findings.title: Possible crash on undefined destructure when destinationCalendar is empty
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` followed by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` will throw a TypeError if destinationCalendar is empty/undefined, since mainHostDestinationCalendar will be undefined and `.integration` access throws. This happens whenever MeetLocationType is used without any destinationCalendar set, breaking booking creation.

findings.title: Looping over multiple destinationCalendar entries can create duplicate calendar events per credential
findings.body: createAllCalendarEvents now iterates over every destinationCalendar entry and, when no credentialId is set, creates an event for every matching credential of that integration type. If multiple destinationCalendar entries share the same integration type (e.g., several hosts using google_calendar without credentialId), this results in duplicate event creation for the same credential across iterations, since there's no dedupe logic tracking which credentials have already been used.

findings.title: Team destination calendars collected only from non-first users but based on isTeamEventType/collective check happening after push
findings.body: teamDestinationCalendars is populated inside teamMemberPromises map (over users.slice(1)) regardless of whether isTeamEventType is COLLECTIVE at the time of iteration, relying on the outer `isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE"` check inside the callback. This is correct logically, but the subsequent push after evt creation (`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`) mutates the array only if eventType.destinationCalendar or organizerUser.destinationCalendar existed to seed the initial array; if both are null, `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` and `?.push` silently no-ops, meaning team hosts' destination calendars for a collective event are silently dropped when the organizer and event type have no destination calendar configured — which defeats the purpose of this PR (handling collective multi-host destinationCalendar).

findings.title: credential.id passed as externalId-like second positional arg but used as credentialId in createEvent signature mismatch risk
findings.body: createEvent now accepts credentialId as the second parameter in CalendarManager.createEvent, but the exported function `createEvent(credential, calEvent, externalId?)` passes `credential.id` to `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` while naming its own third param `externalId` (unused for that purpose) — the externalId parameter added to the outer createEvent signature is only used for the returned EventResult.externalId field, not forwarded to the calendar.createEvent call, which may cause confusion/maintenance bugs since externalId used for the per-calendar event isn't actually threaded through to the lower level createEvent engines (e.g., Google uses credentialId to find calendar id instead of using passed externalId).

findings.title: updateEvent selectedCalendar lookup compares externalId to itself making filter useless
findings.body: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` — since externalCalendarId is already truthy-checked in the ternary's other branch, this fallback branch only executes when externalCalendarId is falsy, meaning the `find` predicate `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` compares against undefined/empty, which will basically never match any destinationCalendar entry. This logic appears broken: it can never find the right calendar as a fallback, so updateEvent calendarId resolution silently fails back to undefined for all cases where externalCalendarId isn't passed in directly, same for deleteEvent (line 317) and CalendarService.ts's listCalendars via similar logic in packages/lib/CalendarService.ts and larkcalendar's code.
